newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Crucial Russian privatization still ahead - study.
newsitem.headline: Crucial Russian privatization still ahead - study.

text.p: The future of many of Russia's biggest enterprises hangs on significant state holdings that have yet to be privatised, a new study by a U.S. reseach team suggested Wednesday.
Joseph Blasi, a professor at Rutgers University, said that major stakes in 24 of Russia's largest 100 companies remained in government hands.
"The average state ownership (in these companies) is 20 percent -- privatisation is still unfinished," he said.

Blasi, whose Russian Research Project is studying the top 100 companies, a follow-up to a multi-year study of 18,000 Russian companies, said the remaining privatisation would define the companies' futures.
"Whoever gets this leftover ownership will probably become a kingmaker," he said.
Management and workers own an average 22 percent stake in top companies, 58 percent is owned by outsiders and 21 percent is owned by the state, he said.

Shareholders and management are often at odds, he said, adding that 49 percent of all outside shareholders with more than a 5 percent stake at the companies studied so far were under-represented or not represented on boards of directors.
"Every company is involved in a shareholder conflict, whether under-the-surface tension, a lawsuit or a dispute of some kind."
Changes at the newly-privatised firms had not been deep, the study showed.
"The pattern is that a lot (of companies) engage in some restructuring behaviour but the effect on sales is generally very modest," said Blasi.
